name: Turn off Click to Do
summary: Remove the screen analysis overlay that offers actions on what is on screen.
what: Sets the policy Disable Click to Do. Click to Do takes a screenshot of the screen when you start it and analyzes it on the device to offer actions. With the policy on, the component and the places that start it are not available.
benefit: Nothing can capture and analyze your screen through Click to Do, and its shortcuts and menu entries stop doing anything.
risk: Low. Copy text out of images and the other quick actions of Click to Do are gone until you revert.
advice: Suggested if you do not use Click to Do. Skip it if you copy text from images with it.
facts: Microsoft says the analysis runs on the device and Click to Do cannot take screenshots while it is closed
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Turn off the Settings agentic search
summary: Keep the natural language AI search in Settings turned off.
what: Sets the policy Disable Settings agentic search experience. With it on, Settings search is limited to its indexed and semantic results and does not use an AI model to suggest settings.
benefit: Settings search stays a plain search and what you type there is not handed to an AI model.
risk: None. Searching Settings by name keeps working.
advice: Suggested if you prefer a plain Settings search. It only matters on builds that have the agentic search.
facts: Microsoft's policy file lists Pro, Enterprise and Education, and reports differ on whether Pro honors it
Nothing breaks if an edition ignores it
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account

name: Keep Windows agent connectors off
summary: Stop AI agents from reaching Windows tools and files through agent connectors.
what: Sets the policy Configure Agent Connectors to Force Disable. Agent connectors let AI agents on the PC talk to tools and apps that Windows offers them.
benefit: No agent can use a Windows agent connector, and nobody can turn them on from Settings while the policy is set.
risk: Low. Only AI agent features that depend on connectors are affected, and they are experimental.
advice: Suggested if you want AI agents kept away from your PC. It is a guard, since the feature is off by default.
facts: Microsoft lists the choices as User is in control, Force Enable and Force Disable
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Block apps from using Windows text and image generation (all accounts)
summary: Force app access to the text and image generation features of Windows off for every account.
what: Applies the app privacy policy Let Windows apps make use of Text and image generation features of Windows and sets it to Force Deny. Nobody can turn it back on in Settings.
benefit: No Windows app on this PC can call the built in generation features, and nobody can change that from Settings.
risk: Low. Apps that offer rewrite or image tools through Windows lose them. The Settings switch is locked until you revert.
advice: Suggested only for shared or locked down PCs, or if you never use the built in writing and image tools.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Users cannot change it from Settings while it is on
Policies are honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: No app promotions in the Share window
summary: Stop the Share window from suggesting apps to install.
what: Sets the policy that stops the Windows Share window from showing promotional app suggestions.
benefit: The Share window lists only what you can share to, with no suggested apps.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone. You lose nothing you need.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: No Microsoft 365 Copilot prompt at sign-in
summary: Stop Windows from launching Microsoft 365 Copilot setup guidance when you sign in.
what: Sets the Cloud Content policy Disable Copilot Pin Screen. Microsoft says it stops the Microsoft 365 Copilot setup guidance from launching at sign-in and does not disable Copilot or change licensing.
benefit: No Copilot recommendation window after you sign in.
risk: None. Copilot itself and any license are not touched.
advice: Suggested for everyone who does not want a Copilot prompt at sign-in.
facts: Microsoft does not say which editions honor it, and the other Cloud Content policies are honored on Enterprise and Education only
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account

name: Turn off the compatibility scan for backed up apps
summary: Stop Windows from scanning installed apps for compatibility problems after a backup.
what: Sets the policy Turn off compatibility scan for backed up applications. The scan evaluates installed applications for compatibility problems and is skipped with the policy on.
benefit: One less background scan of what is installed on the PC.
risk: None. Apps run the same and only the backup compatibility report is not made.
advice: Suggested if you do not use Windows Backup to move apps to a new PC.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Keep your email and name off the sign-in screen
summary: Stop the sign-in screen from showing your email address or user name.
what: Sets the policy Block user from showing account details on sign-in, so nobody can choose to show the email address or user name there.
benefit: A shared screen, a stream or a photo of the sign-in screen does not give away your account name.
risk: Low. You must remember your account name, since the sign-in screen no longer shows it to you.
advice: Suggested for shared or public PCs and for streaming. Skip it if you forget which account you use.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Stop new tray icons popping onto the taskbar
summary: Keep newly added notification icons from being shown on the taskbar for a while.
what: Sets the policy Turn off automatic promotion of notification icons to the taskbar for your account. New icons stay where Windows puts them until you choose.
benefit: A newly installed app does not push its icon onto the taskbar by itself.
risk: None. You can still show or hide every icon in Settings.
advice: Your choice. It only stops icons from appearing on their own.
facts: Users can still show or hide icons in Settings

name: Stop Edge downloading its on device AI model
summary: Keep Edge from downloading and storing a local generative AI model.
what: Applies the Edge policy Settings for GenAI local foundational model and sets it to Disallowed. Microsoft says the model is not downloaded, and one that is already there is deleted.
benefit: Saves the disk space and the download, and no local model is used for Edge features.
risk: Low. Edge features that run an AI model on the device are not available. Edge may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Suggested if you do not use Edge's AI features.
facts: Revert removes the policy value, and Edge may download the model again

name: Remove the news feed from Edge's new tab page
summary: Show a plain new tab page with no Microsoft content below the search box.
what: Applies the Edge policy Allow Microsoft content on the new tab page and turns it off. The content control on the page is set to Content off and cannot be changed.
benefit: No news feed, promoted stories or sponsored cards on every new tab.
risk: None. Quick links and the background picture are separate settings.
advice: Suggested for everyone who does not read the feed. Edge may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
facts: Applies to every profile, signed in or not

name: Stop Edge Spotlight pictures, tips and notices
summary: Turn off the customized backgrounds, suggestions, notifications and tips Edge shows for Microsoft services.
what: Applies the Edge policy Choose whether users can receive customized background images and text, suggestions, notifications, and tips for Microsoft services, set to off.
benefit: Fewer Microsoft suggestions and notices inside the browser.
risk: None. Edge may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Suggested for everyone who finds the tips and suggestions distracting.
facts: Takes effect the next time Edge starts

name: Stop the controller button opening Game Bar
summary: Keep the Xbox button on a controller from opening Game Bar over your game.
what: Sets the per account value behind the Game Bar option Open Xbox Game Bar using this button on a controller to off.
benefit: A press of the guide button no longer throws a Game Bar overlay on top of the game or the desktop.
risk: None. Game Bar still opens with Win+G.
advice: Suggested if you play with a controller and the overlay gets in the way.
facts: Writes the value the Game Bar settings page does, which Microsoft does not document

name: Stop Windows changing your default printer
summary: Keep your chosen default printer instead of the one you used last.
what: Sets the per account value behind the Settings switch Let Windows manage my default printer to off.
benefit: The default printer stays the one you picked, not whichever printer you printed to last.
risk: None. You choose the default printer yourself again.
advice: Suggested if you use more than one printer and want one to stay the default.
facts: Writes the value the Printers and scanners page does, which Microsoft does not document

name: Compact spacing in File Explorer
summary: Fit more files on screen by tightening the space between items.
what: Turns on the File Explorer option Decrease space between items (compact view) for your account.
benefit: More rows of a folder fit on one screen, which helps with long lists.
risk: None. Touch use gets smaller targets.
advice: Your choice. It changes only how tight the file list looks.

name: Show the full folder path in the File Explorer title
summary: Put the whole path of the open folder in the window title.
what: Turns on the File Explorer option Display the full path in the title bar for your account.
benefit: The window title and the taskbar preview name the full folder path, which helps when several windows are open.
risk: None.
advice: Your choice. It changes only the window title.
facts: Applies to File Explorer windows opened afterward

name: Virtual Machine Platform
summary: The light virtualization layer that WSL 2 and many emulators need.
what: Turns on the Virtual Machine Platform optional feature. It is the part of Windows virtualization that does not need the full Hyper-V role.
benefit: WSL 2 and other tools that run virtual machines or Android apps can start.
risk: Low. Needs a restart and virtualization turned on in the firmware. It can change how some older virtual machine tools run beside it.
advice: Suggested only if a tool you use asks for it, such as WSL 2.
facts: Needs hardware virtualization enabled in the firmware
Windows Subsystem for Linux 2 needs it

name: Windows Hypervisor Platform
summary: Lets third party virtual machine and emulator software use the Windows hypervisor.
what: Turns on the Windows Hypervisor Platform optional feature, an interface that other virtualization software can use.
benefit: Emulators and virtual machine tools that support it can run with hardware acceleration while Windows virtualization is on.
risk: Low. Needs a restart and virtualization turned on in the firmware. Running the hypervisor can cost some game performance on certain PCs.
advice: Suggested only if a tool you use asks for it, such as an Android emulator.
facts: Needs hardware virtualization enabled in the firmware

name: Block apps from using Windows text and image generation (this account)
summary: Turn off app access to the text and image generation features of Windows for your account.
what: Sets the per account app permission behind Settings, Privacy and security, Text and image generation to Deny.
benefit: Apps that ask Windows for its on device writing and image tools cannot use them until you allow it again.
risk: Low. Rewrite and image tools inside Notepad, Paint, Photos and similar apps stop working. Allow it again in Settings.
advice: Suggested if you do not use the built in writing and image tools. Most people should use this one and not the all accounts version.
facts: Per account, so other accounts are not affected
The all accounts policy locks the same page in Settings, which was seen on a PC that had it set
Microsoft does not document the value, and its name matches the policy it belongs to
Revert restores exactly what was there before

name: Hide Gallery in the File Explorer sidebar
summary: Take the Gallery entry out of the navigation pane.
what: Unpins the Gallery shell folder from the navigation pane of File Explorer for your account.
benefit: One less entry in the sidebar for a view of pictures that many people never open.
risk: None. Your pictures stay where they are.
advice: Your choice. It changes only the sidebar.
facts: Microsoft does not document the value, which is the one the shell folder itself reads

name: Hide Home in the File Explorer sidebar
summary: Take the Home entry out of the navigation pane.
what: Unpins the Home shell folder from the navigation pane of File Explorer for your account.
benefit: A sidebar that starts at your own folders and drives, without the recent and recommended files page.
risk: None. Pair it with Open File Explorer to This PC so a new window does not open on a page that is gone.
advice: Your choice. It changes only the sidebar.
facts: Microsoft does not document the value, which is the one the shell folder itself reads

name: Do not reopen apps when you sign back in
summary: Stop Windows from saving your open apps and starting them again after a restart.
what: Turns off the sign-in option Automatically save my restartable apps and restart them when I sign back in, for your account.
benefit: After a restart you get a clean desktop, with no apps coming back that you had closed in your head.
risk: None. You open your apps yourself.
advice: Suggested if apps keep coming back after a restart. It is already off on most PCs.
facts: Read back from the real registry here by turning the Settings switch on and off

name: Do not sign in automatically after an update restart
summary: Stop Windows from holding your sign-in to finish setting up after a restart.
what: Sets the policy Sign-in and lock last interactive user automatically after a restart to off, which is the policy behind Use my sign-in info to automatically finish setting up after an update.
benefit: After a restart nobody is signed in until you sign in, and your account is not signed in behind the lock screen.
risk: Low. Apps you had open are not brought back after an update, and some updates finish their setup after you sign in.
advice: Suggested on shared or portable PCs. Skip it if you want the PC ready as soon as it restarts.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Microsoft says it is on by default when the policy is not set
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: No snap layouts when you hover over Maximize
summary: Stop the layout picker from opening when the pointer rests on the Maximize button.
what: Unticks the Multitasking option Show snap layouts when I hover over a window's maximize button, for your account.
benefit: A pointer that passes over Maximize no longer opens a panel of layouts.
risk: None. Win+Z and dragging a window still snap it.
advice: Your choice. It only stops a panel from opening.
facts: Read back from the real registry here by ticking the Settings option and unticking it

name: No suggestions after you snap a window
summary: Stop Windows from offering other windows to fill the rest of the screen.
what: Unticks the Multitasking option When I snap a window, suggest what I can snap next to it, for your account.
benefit: Snapping one window leaves the other half of the screen alone instead of showing a picker.
risk: None. You can still snap a second window yourself.
advice: Your choice. It only stops a picker from appearing.
facts: Read back from the real registry here by ticking the Settings option and unticking it

name: Stop the finish setting up your device reminders
summary: Turn off the prompts that suggest ways to get the most out of Windows.
what: Turns off the Notifications option Suggest ways to get the most out of Windows and finish setting up this device, for your account.
benefit: No full screen or toast prompts asking you to finish setup, sign in to a Microsoft account or try a service.
risk: None. Every feature stays in Settings.
advice: Suggested for everyone. You lose nothing you need.
facts: Guides name this value for that option, and Microsoft does not document it

name: Turn off cloud optimized content
summary: Make Windows show its plain default content where it would pull cloud content.
what: Sets the Cloud Content policy Turn off cloud optimized content. Windows experiences that use the cloud optimized content component show their default fallback content instead.
benefit: Less content chosen and delivered by Microsoft in Windows surfaces, such as tips and promotions.
risk: None. The surfaces still work and show their standard content.
advice: Suggested for everyone. You lose nothing you need.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Microsoft does not say which editions honor it, and the other Cloud Content policies are honored on Enterprise and Education only

name: Turn off the Get Started experience
summary: Stop Windows from launching its Get Started guidance by itself.
what: Sets the Cloud Content policy Disable Get Started. Get Started does not launch automatically and closes at once if opened by hand, and its background tasks do not run.
benefit: No welcome and learn about Windows prompts after setup or an update.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone who does not want the guided tour.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Microsoft does not say which editions honor it, and the other Cloud Content policies are honored on Enterprise and Education only

name: Stop File Explorer showing cloud recommended files
summary: Keep File Explorer from asking the cloud for files based on your account activity.
what: Sets the policy Show files based on your account and cloud provider activity to off. File Explorer stops requesting cloud file metadata for the Home page and views such as Recent, Recommended, Favorites and Shared.
benefit: The Home page no longer fills with files Microsoft or OneDrive picked for you, and Explorer makes fewer cloud requests.
risk: Low. Cloud based Recommended and Shared lists in File Explorer stay empty.
advice: Suggested if you do not use the recommended files in File Explorer.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Turn off feature advertisement notifications
summary: Hide notification balloons that Windows marks as feature advertisements.
what: Sets the policy Turn off feature advertisement balloon notifications for your account.
benefit: Fewer balloons that advertise Windows features.
risk: None. Other notifications are not touched.
advice: Suggested for everyone. You lose nothing you need.

name: Keep OneDrive quiet until you sign in to it
summary: Stop the OneDrive sync program from using the network before you sign in to OneDrive.
what: Sets the OneDrive policy that prevents OneDrive.exe from generating network traffic, such as checking for updates, until you sign in to OneDrive or start syncing files.
benefit: A PC where OneDrive is installed but not used makes no OneDrive network requests.
risk: Low. OneDrive does not start by itself until you sign in to it or choose files to sync.
advice: Suggested if OneDrive is installed and you do not use it.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account

name: Turn off text suggestions on the on-screen keyboard
summary: Stop the word suggestions that appear above the touch keyboard and handwriting panel.
what: Sets two policies for your account, Turn off offer text predictions as I type and Disable text prediction for the Touch Keyboard and Handwriting panel.
benefit: No row of word suggestions while you type on the on-screen keyboard.
risk: None. Typing works the same without the suggestions.
advice: Your choice. Suggested if the suggestion row gets in the way.
facts: Microsoft says the first policy does not stop an app from changing the option itself
The physical keyboard suggestions are a separate setting

name: Turn off autocorrect and misspelling underlines
summary: Stop Windows from correcting and underlining words as you type.
what: Sets two policies for your account, Turn off autocorrect misspelled words and Turn off highlight misspelled words.
benefit: What you type stays as you typed it, and no red lines appear under words in places that use the Windows spelling options.
risk: None. Apps with their own spell check keep it.
advice: Your choice. Suggested if autocorrect changes words you meant to type.
facts: Microsoft says the policies do not stop an app from changing the option itself

name: Never open the touch keyboard by itself
summary: Keep the on-screen keyboard from appearing when you tap a text box.
what: Sets the Typing option Show the touch keyboard to Never for your account.
benefit: No keyboard sliding up over your screen when a touch screen or a missing keyboard makes Windows think you need one.
risk: Low. On a tablet without a keyboard you open the touch keyboard from the taskbar by hand.
advice: Suggested if the touch keyboard appears on a desktop or a laptop that has a keyboard. Skip it on a tablet.
facts: Guides name this value and its 0, 1 and 2 choices, and Microsoft does not document it
It reads 1, which is the When no keyboard is attached choice, on the PC it was found on

name: Turn off typing insights
summary: Stop Windows from keeping a record of your typing to improve suggestions and corrections.
what: Turns off the Typing option Typing insights for your account.
benefit: Windows stops tracking how you type to improve word suggestions and spelling fixes.
risk: None. Suggestions may get less personal.
advice: Suggested if you want less typing data kept on the PC.
facts: Guides name this value and Microsoft does not document it, and it already reads off on the PC it was found on

name: No text suggestions when typing on a physical keyboard
summary: Stop the suggestion bar that can appear while you type on a real keyboard.
what: Turns off the Typing option Show text suggestions when typing on the physical keyboard for your account.
benefit: No popup of word suggestions over what you are typing.
risk: None. Typing works the same.
advice: Your choice. Try it if a suggestion popup appears while you type, and revert it if nothing changes.
facts: The value name comes from guides written for early Windows 11 builds, and it was not read back on this PC or on a current build
Revert restores the earlier value or removes this one

name: Turn off Game Bar recording for every account
summary: Disallow Windows game recording and broadcasting for the whole PC.
what: Sets the policy that enables or disables Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting to disabled. Windows game recording is not allowed for any account.
benefit: No background recording or broadcasting on any account, and it cannot be turned back on from Game Bar settings.
risk: Low. Game Bar clips, the record last 30 seconds feature and broadcasting stop working for everyone.
advice: Suggested if nobody on this PC records gameplay with Game Bar. The per account version is enough for one person.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account

name: Stop the Get an app to open this ms-gamebar link message
summary: Give the Game Bar links a harmless handler, so Windows stops asking you to find an app in the Store.
what: For your account only, registers the ms-gamebar, ms-gamebarservices and ms-gamingoverlay links with a small do nothing Windows program, systray.exe, instead of leaving them with no handler.
benefit: The Get an app to open this ms-gamebar link box that can appear when you use a controller or press a Game Bar key stops appearing on a PC where Xbox Game Bar is removed.
risk: Medium. If Xbox Game Bar is installed, these links no longer open it for your account, and Win+G or the controller button may stop working. Revert removes the handlers.
advice: Use it only when Xbox Game Bar is removed and the message keeps coming back. Skip it if you use Game Bar.
facts: Per account setting, so other accounts are not affected
People report this fixes the message, and it was not tested on a PC where Game Bar is installed
Turning off the controller button and Game Bar recording first removes the usual triggers
Revert removes the handlers it added, and the link keys it created stay empty

name: Turn off Storage Sense
summary: Stop Windows from cleaning files by itself when the disk runs low.
what: Sets the policy Allow Storage Sense to disabled. Storage Sense does not turn on, and it does not remove temporary files, Recycle Bin items or old Downloads files on its own.
benefit: Nothing is deleted behind your back, which matters if you keep files in Downloads or the Recycle Bin.
risk: Low. The disk does not clean itself when it fills up, so Clean up or Settings has to be run by hand.
advice: Suggested if you want to decide what is deleted. Skip it on a small drive that runs low on space.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Microsoft says Storage Sense turns on by itself when the PC runs into low disk space
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Stop PC makers running software at startup
summary: Block the firmware of the PC from starting programs inside Windows at boot.
what: Sets DisableWpbtExecution. The Windows Platform Binary Table lets a PC maker put a program in the firmware that Windows runs at startup, which some makers use to install their own tools again after a clean install.
benefit: A clean Windows install stays clean, without a maker app coming back by itself.
risk: Medium. Anti-theft and recovery software that works this way stops starting, and on some laptops it is how the tool for fan modes, lighting or Fn keys gets installed. Needs a restart.
advice: Suggested only on a desktop or after a clean install where a maker app keeps returning. Skip it if you rely on a maker tool or anti-theft software.
facts: Microsoft documents the table, and its own document does not mention this value
Community tools set this value and it is already set on the PC it was found on
Enforced for every account, and it needs a restart
portableNote: On a laptop, the maker can use this to install the app that handles fan modes, keyboard lighting and Fn keys, and it may not come back once it is blocked.

name: Always show scrollbars
summary: Keep scrollbars on screen instead of hiding them until the pointer moves.
what: Turns off the Accessibility option that hides scrollbars automatically, for your account.
benefit: You can see how long a page is and grab the bar without waiting for it to appear.
risk: None. Windows apps that use their own scrollbars are not affected.
advice: Your choice. It changes only how scrollbars show.
facts: Windows calls it Always show scrollbars under Accessibility, Visual effects
Microsoft does not document the value, and guides name it

name: Turn off window snapping
summary: Stop windows from resizing and docking when you drag them to a screen edge.
what: Turns off the Windows feature that arranges a window when it is dragged to an edge or corner, for your account. It is the same switch as Snap windows under Multitasking.
benefit: A window stays the size you gave it wherever you drop it.
risk: None. Win+Z layouts and the snap shortcuts stop working with it.
advice: Your choice. Suggested if windows keep resizing when you move them near an edge.
facts: Sign out and in for it to take effect
The value belongs to the documented window arranging option, and Microsoft does not name the registry value
